title: Sell Mineral Rights in Judsonia, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Judsonia, AR
metaDescription: Judsonia, AR mineral rights in White County, one of the more heavily drilled parts of the Fayetteville Shale. Legacy leases from the 2000s gas boom.
heroLead: Judsonia sits in White County, one of the counties where the Fayetteville Shale saw its heaviest horizontal drilling, which means most local mineral tracts have some history with the play.
intro: White County was a core part of the Fayetteville Shale's productive fairway, and Southwestern Energy and other operators drilled hundreds of horizontal wells across the county between the mid-2000s and early 2010s. Land around Judsonia was part of that development, and many local mineral owners have received royalty checks, however small, at some point over the past two decades.

sections.heading: Dense Development, Now Mostly Quiet
paragraphs: Compared to some of the smaller communities in the play, Judsonia's proximity to core White County drilling means a higher share of local tracts have an actual production history rather than just an old, never-drilled lease. That production has declined steadily since the boom years, and new drilling activity in the area has been minimal for a long time, which is typical for a mature shale gas play at low gas prices.

sections.heading: What a Producing History Means for Value
paragraphs: A tract with an established, if declining, royalty history gives a buyer real data to work with, which generally makes valuation more straightforward than for an unleased or never-drilled interest. If you have several years of royalty statements, holding onto them helps a buyer assess your interest quickly and accurately.

faqs.question: My Judsonia-area well has been producing since around 2010. Why is the check so much smaller now?
faqs.answer: Fayetteville Shale wells decline steeply in their early years and then level off at a much lower rate, so a well over a decade old typically produces a fraction of its initial output, which is expected.

faqs.question: Is there any chance of new drilling on my tract?
faqs.answer: New Fayetteville Shale drilling has been limited for years due to gas prices, so most current activity in White County is existing production rather than new wells, though that can shift if prices change.

faqs.question: What documents does a buyer need to evaluate my Judsonia interest?
faqs.answer: Your most recent royalty statement or division order, the legal description, and any lease documentation you have. These let a buyer assess both the current production and the underlying mineral value.

faqs.question: Does selling my mineral interest affect my ability to keep the surface property?
faqs.answer: No. Selling mineral rights doesn't affect surface ownership. The two are separate legal interests, and you can sell one while keeping the other.
